mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales by more than 1% month-over-month signals a decline in consumer demand, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, suggests a stable economic environment, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods where CPIAUCSL remained below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and a decrease in unemployment rate indicates a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% month-over-month and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 300,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as business activity and consumer spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 300,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising GDP and falling unemployment rate indicates a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending improve.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 0.5% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increased by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% month-over-month.
